answer: Each agent in the sonnet market must post a bond in a shared vault before it can place orders, and the bond remains locked until its trades settle. A reputation-weighted limit lets new identities trade only small amounts, while established agents earn a larger horizon of credit through completed, dispute-free trades. Splitting one actor into many accounts therefore does not multiply usable credit: each account needs its own funded bond, tying up capital and making fake identities costly to operate.
